title: Data flow diagrams and trust boundaries

videos.script: The first question was: what are we working on? The answer is a drawing. Not an architecture diagram with logos on it. A drawing of where data goes. {{drawing}} Four shapes do it. Somebody outside the system. Code that does something with data. A place where data rests. And an arrow for data moving. {{shapes}} Then a fifth line, dashed, and this is the one that matters. It marks where trust changes. The internet on one side, the clinic's cloud on the other. {{boundary}} Every arrow that crosses that line is a question. Who sent this? Can it be changed on the way? Can it be read? {{crossing}} Today you draw the clinic portal this way, find that eleven of its twelve flows cross a boundary, and write the same drawing as code, so it can live in git beside the system it describes. {{code}}
